data.name: Tiger Hunt
data.detailed_description:
Storm the continent of europe during WWII! You break out of normandy into artillery pounding action, menacing mines and a maelstrom of machine gun fire. Your maneuverable M-4 Sherman tank leads the hard-fought hunt for the enemy. As you push threw fearsome armor piercing German tanks tread lightly as you clear the virtual villages, beaches and farm fields, as the fearsome expert German Tank aces eager to knock your lights out. It takes a tanker like you with courage and cunning to go face to face with the enemy aces and the terrifying tiger tank.

Features:
- Immersive arcade-like explosions and combat clatter.
- Mighty war machines in blueprint precise detail.
- Historically accurate weapons and combat situations.
- Exquisitely detailed virtuial villages, beaches, bridges, railroads, rivers and more...
- Play mission after mission against incredible enemy intelligence.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 98, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, 7
  • Processador: Pentium II 600 MHz
  • Memória: 128 MB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Direct X compatible 16MB video card that supports 16bit graphics
  • DirectX: Versão 8.0
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 320 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: 16 bit sound card.
  • Notas adicionais: Combatability problems can be avoided by setting the executable to run in compatibility mode for windows XP. The .exe files are usually in their respective game folders at \Steam\steamapps\common
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 98, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, 7
  • Processador: Pentium II 866 MHz or higher
  • Memória: 128 MB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: 32MB video card (with hardware T&L support) that supports 16bit graphics
  • DirectX: Versão 8.0
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 320 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: 16 bit sound card.
  • Notas adicionais: Combatability problems can be avoided by setting the executable to run in compatibility mode for windows XP. The .exe files are usually in their respective game folders at \Steam\steamapps\common

reviews.review:
Tiger Hunt delivers an old-school World War II tank combat experience that focuses on explosive battlefield encounters, straightforward vehicle controls, and the challenge of surviving against heavily armed German forces. Developed and published by Digital Fusion Inc., the game puts players in command of an American M4 Sherman tank during the Allied campaign across Western Europe. Instead of emphasizing the demanding technical details of realistic armored warfare, it adopts an arcade-oriented approach that makes combat relatively accessible while retaining elements of tactical positioning. Its greatest appeal comes from the opportunity to participate in historically inspired tank battles, although its aging technology and limited mechanical complexity prevent it from reaching the standards of more sophisticated military games.

The gameplay revolves around navigating hostile environments, identifying enemy positions, and destroying opposing vehicles before they can overwhelm the player's tank. German armor presents the most recognizable threat, particularly the powerful Tiger tanks that give the game its identity. Facing these heavily protected opponents creates situations where careful movement and intelligent positioning become essential. Charging directly into enemy fire is rarely the most effective strategy, and players are encouraged to use the battlefield to their advantage. Nevertheless, the combat remains relatively simple, prioritizing immediate action over detailed ammunition management, realistic armor penetration calculations, or complicated crew operations.

Environmental variety contributes significantly to the overall experience. Battles take place across European landscapes featuring villages, agricultural fields, rivers, bridges, roads, and other recognizable wartime locations. These settings provide different combat situations, from navigating confined settlements to engaging enemy vehicles across more exposed terrain. Obstacles and defensive positions influence how players approach individual encounters, while threats such as mines, artillery, and machine-gun fire help establish the dangers of advancing through hostile territory. Although the environments lack the interactive complexity of modern battlefields, they provide enough variation to support the game's mission-based progression.

One of the more interesting aspects of Tiger Hunt is its emphasis on recognizable military equipment. The Sherman tank serves as the player's primary vehicle, while German armored forces provide opposition through machines associated with some of the most famous tank engagements of the war. This historical foundation gives the action a stronger identity than a completely fictional combat setting. However, the game takes considerable liberties with realism to maintain its accessible gameplay. Vehicle handling, enemy engagements, and battlefield encounters are designed primarily for entertainment rather than strict historical accuracy. Players looking for a demanding tank simulator may therefore find its simplified systems disappointing, while fans of uncomplicated military action may appreciate the reduced learning curve.

Enemy encounters provide much of the game's difficulty. Hostile tanks and defensive installations force players to remain alert, particularly when advancing into unfamiliar areas. The presence of dangerous German opponents creates occasional moments of genuine tension, especially when the player must react quickly to incoming attacks. However, the artificial intelligence reflects the limitations of older action games. Enemy behavior lacks the tactical sophistication expected from contemporary military simulations, and repeated encounters can eventually expose predictable combat patterns. As a result, the difficulty sometimes feels more dependent on enemy placement and firepower than on elaborate battlefield strategy.

Visually, Tiger Hunt has a distinctly dated appearance. Its three-dimensional environments, vehicle models, textures, and explosions reflect an earlier generation of PC gaming. Nevertheless, the recognizable tank designs and varied European scenery provide a reasonable sense of place. The battlefield presentation succeeds in communicating the basic atmosphere of armored warfare without delivering exceptional graphical detail. Explosions and weapon effects add excitement to combat, while mechanical sounds and battlefield noise reinforce the military setting. The audiovisual experience has nostalgic value, but players accustomed to modern graphics, realistic destruction, and immersive sound design will immediately recognize its limitations.

The game's longevity depends largely on how much enjoyment players derive from its core combat loop. Progressing through missions and overcoming increasingly dangerous opposition provides a sense of accomplishment, but the absence of extensive customization, sophisticated progression systems, and modern multiplayer features restricts its replayability. Once the basic mechanics become familiar, there is relatively little to fundamentally change the experience. This makes Tiger Hunt better suited to occasional sessions of nostalgic military action than prolonged playthroughs built around strategic experimentation.

Technical compatibility represents another important consideration. Despite its extremely modest hardware requirements, Tiger Hunt was designed around older Windows systems and legacy graphics technology. Modern computers may encounter launching difficulties, display problems, or other compatibility issues. Running the executable in Windows XP compatibility mode may help resolve certain problems, but successful operation is not guaranteed. These technical inconveniences can diminish the appeal of an otherwise straightforward game, particularly for players expecting a trouble-free experience.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently Unknown or Unverified, with no confirmed official Verified or Playable classification established. Although the handheld possesses more than enough processing power for the game's modest requirements, its older Windows architecture and DirectX dependencies may introduce difficulties when running through Proton. Manual controller configuration could also be necessary. Consequently, Steam Deck owners should not assume reliable functionality without additional testing.

Overall, Tiger Hunt offers a nostalgic journey into classic arcade-style tank warfare, combining recognizable World War II vehicles, varied battlefield environments, and uncomplicated combat mechanics. Its historical inspiration and accessible action remain appealing, but repetitive engagements, outdated visuals, limited tactical depth, and compatibility concerns weaken the overall experience. It is most suitable for enthusiasts of older military games who value simplicity and atmosphere over modern technical refinement. 

Rating: 6/10
